note: Three defenses are recovered from the fed's own 2001 cards, none of which moves the belts: a fifteen-minute time-limit draw against The Professionals at PRIMETIME in Tacoma on 6 October 2001, announced as a draw after the referee had already counted three for the champions; and the champions still billed and defending as of PRIMETIME in New Orleans (11 November) and PRIMETIME in St. Louis (26 December), where they challenge the whole tag division to a gauntlet match at ANNIVERSARY. A FOURTH defense, dated to the day, is the one that challenge was building to: the four-way HOUSE OF PAIN cage match at ANNIVERSARY 2001 on 31 December 2001, in which the champions RETAIN. Michael Hardy takes most of the match's punishment, is spike-tombstoned and busted open, and still scores both of his team's falls -- cradling WJ Mills out of a FrankenParsons to eliminate Raw Deal, then splashing both Professionals off the top of the cage on a Rocket Launcher from Simon Wilcox for the win, with the CS Express on the floor to stop Eddie Mayfield's chairshot first. The fed's own cards call this belt the Unified Tag Team Championships in their section headers and the CSWA World Tag Team Titles in their commentary, within the same document; both readings are recorded and neither is resolved. One of the champions puts the length of this reign at "six months or so" on 26 December 2001, which does not sit with the reign's own recorded start at PRIMETIME in Paducah in February 2001; that disagreement is recorded too. The ANNIVERSARY card adds a THIRD spelling to that first disagreement and resolves nothing: its own section header reads "the CSWA Unified Tag Team Titles" and its commentary "the Unified Tag Team Championships".

conflict.note: SOURCES DISAGREE INSIDE ONE DOCUMENT, resolved by the fed's own later text and recorded rather than quietly dropped. BATTLE OF THE BELTS XIV's own match call has Aaron Reno defending against Michaels, Teri Melton hitting Reno with a Top Rope DDT, and Michaels finishing with a leg drop off the middle rope: "ONE....TWO....THREE!! But that same card's closing recap, written in a different broadcast voice, runs through the night's title changes and calls one of them "a new USN Heavyweight Champion in Aaron Reno" — naming the man who LOST the belt. The registry follows the match call, because the fed's own FISH FUND XI of 6 September 1996 says outright that "Tom Adler took the title from Scotty Michaels", which only holds if Michaels left BATTLE OF THE BELTS XIV as champion. The recap's own words are preserved here.
